Definition: from G2596 and G2749; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal:--keep, lie, sit at meat (down).
BiblicalUsage: To lie down is to be sick in bed, to be laid out where others must carry you, and the Gospels are full of it: the paralytic let down through the roof, the man at the pool who had lain there thirty-eight years, the father of Publius lying sick of a fever, and Levi rising from his table to make Jesus a great feast. The word holds the sickbed and the table together, because Jesus meets people in both places.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus still comes to the sickbed first, because He saw the man lying there and knew how long it had been. I hold that the same Lord who lifts the sick also sits at the table with sinners, and I am glad He does both.
